reason: The immediate goal is to put the station on reserve, so connecting the charged battery at the shutdown controls seems like the most direct first step.
expectation: I expect the station to switch to its emergency reserve, though other shutdown actions may still be needed.

alternatives.reason: The outdoor water line will lose heat, so its shutdown also seems relevant, but I want to secure reserve power first.
Moving the heat store would help protect the garden, but the stated first goal is station reserve.

effect: The reserve now powers essential loads, while the fuel plant and normal garden circulation are off. The water line still needs attention before I move the garden into the nook.
reaction: The dimmed lights make the switch to survival mode feel immediate.
reason: The outdoor water line will lose its heat, so I want to address it at the shutdown controls before protecting the garden.
expectation: I expect this to shut down or isolate the outdoor water line, though I don't know exactly how the station will protect it.

alternatives.reason: The heat store could help protect the garden, but the exposed water line also needs attention.

effect: The outdoor line is drained and isolated, with its pump and thaw checks on reserve power. The station is now on its planned reserve, and the next goal is to move both troughs into the nook.
reaction: Draining the line makes sense now that its heating will be lost.
reason: The charged heat store should help keep the nook warm for the troughs, so I want to place it before moving them.
expectation: I expect the heat store to release warmth inside the nook, though I don't know whether placing it will advance the trough-moving goal.

alternatives.reason: Moving the lettuce directly addresses the new goal, but I want the heat store in place first.
The potato trough also needs shelter, but the heat store may help protect both beds.

effect: The heat store is now in the growing nook, creating a buffered space; both troughs still need to be moved.
reaction: The result is brief, so I am unsure how much warmth the store will provide.
reason: Moving the lettuce trough directly advances the goal of sheltering both beds.
expectation: I expect the lettuce trough to be placed inside the buffered nook, with the potato trough still to follow.

alternatives.reason: The potato trough also needs to move; either bed seems reasonable to move first.

effect: The lettuce is sheltered with its reservoir intact and the common-return couplings capped. The potato trough still needs to be moved.
reaction: Carrying the bed level and protecting its leaves makes the move feel practical.
reason: Moving the potato trough is the only remaining combination and completes the stated task of moving both beds.
expectation: I expect the potato trough to be placed in the buffered nook alongside the lettuce, though it may need further care afterward.

effect: Both troughs are now sheltered in the nook with their reservoirs, and the chapter is complete.
reaction: The attention to the potato bed's cover, support and leaves made the move feel practical.

mostWorthwhile.text: Draining and isolating the outdoor water line was the most worthwhile action: it connected the loss of heating to a concrete protective measure while keeping thaw checks powered.

leastWorthwhile.text: Placing the heat store felt least informative because the result only named a buffered nook without explaining its effect.

surprise.text: Switching to reserve also stopped normal garden circulation, making the nook's low-power outlets relevant.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the heat store's placement made sense, although its brief result left its contribution unclear.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because I want to see how the station and its specimens fare through the storm, though this chapter's final moves were fairly predictable.
